episode_title: AI Is Confidently Wrong. Ask Who Built It Before You Buy.
question: Why is AI confidently wrong according to software developers building chiropractic tools?
transcript_excerpt: According to Miles Bodzin, AI is confidently wrong all the time. Every bit of development he does, he finds errors in what it is doing and has to push back. The only way he can push back is because he knows what he is looking for and knows how to write software. His concern is that entrepreneurial chiropractors will build things using AI and bring them to the profession, but the profession does not know any better, resulting in a lot of problematic products in the marketplace.

episode_title: AI Is Confidently Wrong. Ask Who Built It Before You Buy.
question: What security and quality risks does Miles Bodzin warn about with AI-built chiropractic products?
transcript_excerpt: Bodzin warns there will be a lot of crap in the marketplace and stuff being brought to market that does not have a lot of security in it. Even with engineers and smart people running software companies, there are still bugs and problems. When Joe Average person builds something, it will be riddled with problems. He cautions that chiropractors buying these products should ask: How was it built? Were there engineers? Were there people who knew what they were doing, or was it just Joe friend down the street who built something?

episode_title: AI Is Confidently Wrong. Ask Who Built It Before You Buy.
question: How can Cash Practice AI help chiropractors retain patients through awareness of patient adherence?
transcript_excerpt: Cash Practice's AI platform is aware of what is happening with patients—not only their outcomes but whether they are falling off track with their adherence to care plans and when they have key milestones coming up. The platform can communicate signals that a patient is showing signs of attrition or falling off track before they are already gone. This helps chiropractors keep patients informed and engaged by force-multiplying the doctor and team to retain patients, rather than replacing human interaction.

episode_title: AI Is Confidently Wrong. Ask Who Built It Before You Buy.
question: What does Miles Bodzin advise chiropractors to ask before buying AI solutions?
transcript_excerpt: Bodzin advises chiropractors to pause and ask questions before buying something marketed to them: How was it built? Who designed it? If the answer is just AI or a chiropractor friend who built something, that is a red flag. He emphasizes that if you are building something for yourself, you only have yourself to look at, but if you are buying from somewhere else, you must ask questions. You cannot just accept it because it looks shiny and pretty—you have to really dig.

episode_title: AI Is Confidently Wrong. Ask Who Built It Before You Buy.
question: How long has Miles Bodzin been working with chiropractors and what was his innovation?
transcript_excerpt: Bodzin has been serving chiropractors for around 20 years with Cash Practice. He was the first to make a recurring revenue model a real thing in chiropractic by enabling credit card billing on file, which was cutting-edge at the time and a game changer for the profession.
